cases.quote: For tab setting, it is necessary to identify tab positions, tab types (how to align the characters in the tab position), and the characters to be set. For this purpose, it is necessary to insert a tab sign before the tabbed character. The series of characters just after the tab sign are the target characters (see Figure 161). If there is more than one tab sign, it is necessary to set the same numbers of tab positions and tab types as the number of tab signs.
cases.rationale: The rule states three declarations per tab sign — a tab position, a tab type, and where the target characters begin — and a precondition on their count: as many declared positions and types as there are signs. This case declares exactly two of each for two signs (`tab_starts` names item 0 and item 1 as where the two target runs begin; `tab_stops` names two start-alignment positions), satisfying the precondition exactly rather than with a surplus, so `jlreq_line::tab_line` never has occasion to refuse it. The first run (item 0 alone, 800 units) seats at the first declared position (0, start-aligned, so its own anchor is the position itself): placements [0], extent 800 — the floor the second run's own search reads. The second run (item 1 alone, 1200 units) then finds the second declared position (800) is the first one that does not fall short of that floor — it matches exactly — and seats there: placements [800], extent 800 plus 1200, 2000. Neither item carries a Table 1 term of its own (cl-19 against cl-19 is a blank cell), so nothing beyond the two declared positions moves either placement. What this case does not exercise is the declared-count precondition's own failure mode: §3.6.1's own words state that fewer positions than signs is a malformed declaration, real in `jlreq_line::tab_line` as `Err(ComposeError::InsufficientTabStops)`, but the published case format has no field for asserting that a call is expected to be refused (`docs/design/conformance.md`'s own unmet bullet on an `expect.refused` shape) — `docs/conformance-deferrals.toml`'s own entry for this rule states that scope limit rather than leaving it implied by a case that stops just short of it.

forbidden.why: The two declared positions are read in the order the two tab signs appear — one position per sign, per §3.6.1's own declared-count sentence — not reused for more than one target run apiece. Both runs anchoring at the first position contradicts that pairing; the second run's own search consumes the second declared position (800) instead, which is also the one that clears the floor the first run leaves and the first position (0) does not.
